props.name: reduced ZnO-Cr2O3 mixture (industrial methanol catalyst)
props.description: The catalyst generally used in industry for methanol synthesis according to the introduction: a reduced mixture of ZnO and Cr2O3, possibly with small additions of other metal oxides.

props.name: ZnO-Cr2O3 pellets with graphite (plant catalyst)
props.description: Catalyst of the designed (German-type) methanol plant: pellets made from ZnO, Cr2O3, water and graphite; composition as charged 26-30% Cr2O3, 59-64% ZnO, 1-1.5% graphite, 9-10% water (basis of the percentages not stated).

props.name: American methanol process
props.note: cited from ref. (1), Ind. Eng. Chem. 40 (1948), 2230
props.statement: In the American process (350 atm, 400 °C) the synthesis gas is made by partial oxidation of natural gas; sulfur is removed with an absorption tower filled with ZnO; cold gas is injected into the catalyst beds to hold the local temperature (to guard against CH4 formation); a purge prevents accumulation of CH4, CO2 and inert gases; the crude methanol contains 74.7% CH3OH, 25% water, plus dimethyl ether, higher alcohols and ketones.

props.name: catalyst life 6 months to 1 year, renewed at 20 atm pressure drop
props.statement: The catalyst life is 6 months to 1 year; the catalyst must be renewed when the pressure drop in the converter reaches 20 atm (12-14 atm with new catalyst), at which point 60-70% of the catalyst has been pulverized.

props.name: cold-gas injection between the beds controls the temperature
props.statement: Part of the synthesis gas bypasses the heat exchanger and is injected cold into the mixing chambers below the catalyst beds to control the converter temperature.

props.name: sudden pressure-drop changes increase unwanted products
props.statement: A constant pressure drop must be kept in the converter, because a sudden variation of only a few atmospheres increases the amount of undesired products.

props.name: CO conversion 12-16% per pass; 72% methanol in the crude
props.note: design figures of the German-type plant; the report does not say how they were obtained
props.statement: The conversion is 12-16% of the CO fed to the converter; the methanol content (yield) of the crude product is 72%.

props.name: pressure correction of cp inconsistent with Perry's N2 chart
props.statement: The enthalpy-based pressure correction made cp smaller at high pressure and more so at lower temperature, whereas Perry's figure for N2 shows cp larger at lower temperature; this does not agree. Since cp varies little for N2 around 250 atm and 200-400 °C and enters the film coefficient as cp^0.3, the pressure effect on cp was neglected.

props.note: cited from ref. (2), FIAT Final Rep. nr. 888
props.statement: In the German process (260 atm, 360-390 °C) water gas is made richer in H2 by converting part of the CO with H2O and washing out the CO2 formed; sulfur and Fe-carbonyl are removed in an absorption tower filled with active carbon; the converter has 6 catalyst beds with cold-gas injection; the crude methanol contains 90% CH3OH, 6-8% water, plus dimethyl ether, higher alcohols and ketones.

props.name: design follows the German process
props.statement: Because predecessors had already treated the American process, it was decided to work out the German system in this design.

props.name: comparison of the German and American processes
props.statement: The American process is simpler (no separate heat exchanger and start heater, one distillation column fewer), while the German process gives a much purer crude product (90% CH3OH against 75%) and is more expensive in equipment; both have equal efficiency. The Germans state that a distillation section as built is needed for methanol pure enough for formaldehyde synthesis.

props.name: industrial methanol synthesis conditions
props.statement: Industrial methanol is generally made by catalytic reduction of CO with H2 at high temperature and pressure (CO + 2H2 -> CH3OH + 21800 cal), starting from an H2:CO mixture of about 2:1, usually at 200-300 atm and about 400 °C, over a reduced mixture of ZnO and Cr2O3, possibly with small amounts of other metal oxides.

props.name: KMnO4 treatment oxidizes Fe-carbonyl in the methanol
props.note: the temperature limit is printed '300 C' in the text layer, probably 30 °C (degree sign lost); both readings are possible
props.statement: In the distillation section, a 1% KMnO4 solution (0.3% of the liquid) oxidizes some organic products and Fe-carbonyl; the temperature must stay below the printed '300 C', otherwise methanol is oxidized.

props.name: methanation sets in above about 400 °C and runs away
props.statement: The side reaction CO + 3H2 -> CH4 + H2O (+59700 cal) occurs when the temperature exceeds about 400 °C; since the main reaction is exothermic, good temperature control is needed. Methanation is even more exothermic than the main reaction: once it starts, the temperature rises increasingly.

props.name: pure-methanol yield about 89% of the methanol in the crude
props.statement: The yield of pure methanol, based on the methanol content of the crude methanol, is about 89%; per ton of crude methanol 780-830 kg pure methanol, 30-100 kg V-methanol, 20 kg dimethyl ether and 0.2-0.3 kg higher alcohols are obtained.

props.name: recycle with purge of inert gases
props.statement: The non-condensed gases are recycled and a part is purged to prevent accumulation of inert gases; the purge at a production of 100 ton methanol is 45,000 m3 gas per day (normal p and t), correcting the 450,000 m3 printed on p. 6.

props.name: the start heater is also needed during operation
props.statement: Since the converter inlet temperature must be 340 °C while the heat exchanger heats the gas only to 263 °C, the start heater is needed not only at start-up but also during operation to bring the synthesis gas to temperature.

props.name: sulfur removal on active carbon with NH3 and O2
props.statement: The fresh gas first passes sulfur-absorption tower 1 (two towers, one in use and one reserve; inside diameter 800 mm, height 8 m, each with a 4 m column of active carbon of density 550 g/liter and particle size 7-10 mm). About 0.5 g NH3 per m3 gas and a little more than the stoichiometric amount of O2 are dosed beforehand as catalyst and oxidant for the sulfur compounds; H2S is oxidized (with air, NH3 as catalyst, alkaline medium) at room temperature and the sulfur is deposited on the active carbon, which must be regenerated after some time by extraction (e.g. with CS2, chlorobenzene, or very suitably an (NH4)2S solution) and then dried with steam and N2.

props.name: synthesis gas to the converter (fresh + recycled gas)
props.description: Fresh gas mixed with the recycled gas in the circulator (recycle about 8 times the fresh gas); passes the oil separator, heat exchanger and start heater to the converter. Inert gases counted as N2 in the calculations.

props.name: methanol converter 3 (design, 6 catalyst beds with cold-gas injection)
props.description: Designed converter: steel shell, inside diameter 800 mm, length 12 m, lined with brass (supplement p. 29: shell 250-300 mm thick; N8- or N5-steel lining 10 mm, brass lining 2 mm, 10 mm free space, brass jacket 2 mm, kieselguhr insulation 70 mm, copper-manganese jacket 12-15 mm); 6 catalyst beds on N8-steel grids covered with copper-manganese, with mixing chambers below each bed where cold gas is injected to control the temperature; thermocouples at several points.
